topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer genetics and cellular transformation.

topics.label: Tumor virology and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of infectious tumor viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and established experimental assays to test cell transformation.

topics.label: Functional classifications and mechanisms of cancer mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles distinguishing oncogenes from tumor suppressor genes through pathways like Rb and dominant-negative mechanisms like mutant p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how failures in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how stepwise mutation accumulation drives tumor evolution in both sporadic progression models and inherited cancer syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session by summarizing learning outcomes, taking questions, and recommending further reading.
